A resurfacing campaign generates sequences that do not exist in nature. No
meaningful multiple sequence alignment exists for a designed HMA variant, so
only the no-MSA results bear on the intended application.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../bin")
from _analysis_common import *

d = load(verbose=False)
df, pred, rt, near, lookup = d["df"], d["pred"], d["rt"], d["near"], d["lookup"]
iface = pd.read_csv(DATA_DIR / "predicted_interfaces_plddt.csv")
```

## Everything on one page

```{python}
rows = []
for (m, f), g in df.groupby(["model", "msa"]):
    if f != "no_msa" or is_oracle(m):
        continue          # reference-restrained runs are not predictors
    acc = g[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD

    sel = []
    for pdb, gp in pred[(pred["model"] == m) & (pred["msa"] == f)].groupby("pdb"):
        gp = gp.dropna(subset=["plddt"])
        if len(gp):
            sel.append({"oracle": gp[RA_COL].min() < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD,
                        "plddt": gp.loc[gp["plddt"].idxmax(), RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD})
    sel = pd.DataFrame(sel)

    n = fl = 0
    for _, r in near.iterrows():
        A, B = lookup.get((m, f, r["pdb_a"])), lookup.get((m, f, r["pdb_b"]))
        if A is None or B is None:
            continue
        n += 1
        fl += ((A[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD) != (B[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD))
    p_ = float(acc.mean())

    ifc = iface[(iface["model"] == m) & (iface["msa"] == f) & (iface["pdb"] != "6Q76")]
    r_ = rt[(rt["model"] == m) & (rt["msa"] == f)]

    rows.append({
        "model": DISPLAY.get(m, m),
        "correct /18 (oracle)": int(acc.sum()),
        "selected by pLDDT": f"{100 * sel['plddt'].mean():.0f}%",
        "consistency": round(2 * p_ * (1 - p_) * n - fl, 1),
        "correct site /13": int((ifc["site"] == "correct site").sum()),
        "AVR-Pia site /13": int((ifc["site"] == "AVR-Pia site").sum()),
        "min/run": round(float(r_["elapsed_min"].median()), 1),
        "peak GB": round(float(r_["peak_rss_gb"].median()), 1),
    })
pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("correct /18 (oracle)", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
```

## What the benchmark says

AlphaFold3 and ESMFold2 are the strongest no-MSA models. They lead on oracle
accuracy, retain the most after pLDDT-based selection, place the most effectors
on the correct surface, and AlphaFold3 is the fastest model in the panel.

Boltz-2 is weak at selection rather than generation. Its oracle accuracy is
respectable, but it shows the largest drop from oracle to pLDDT-selected of any
credible model. It produces good poses and fails to recognise them. Most of its
unprompted picks land on the AVR-Pia surface, so its out-of-the-box output is
the weakest of the serious contenders.

Boltz-2 wins on two axes. It is the most self-consistent across near-identical
inputs, which is the property a resurfacing campaign depends on most, and it has
the smallest memory footprint. Neither outweighs the accuracy gap alone.

The constrained variants are absent from this table. Their restraints come from
the reference complex, so they cannot run on a novel target and do not belong in
a ranking of predictors.

Eighteen complexes from two NLR families is a small sample, and several of these
margins rest on a handful of targets.

## Boltz-2 is steerable, and that is the point

Given contact and pocket restraints derived from the true interface, Boltz-2
improves sharply. Boltz-1 given the same information barely moves.

This is a positive control rather than a result about prediction. It establishes
that Boltz-2 responds to being told where the interface is. Any steering method
depends on that premise, and Boltz-1 shows it is not guaranteed.
